title: Client snapback: late-chunk attribution, partial-output healing, and disconnect tolerance for hosted SSE
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (notably Acme Payments and Skylark SaaS) reported truncated or duplicated tokens when a hosted SSE connection disconnects and then reconnects. Symptoms include partial transcript visible to SDK users, later arrival of one or more 'late chunks' that are not stitched into the visible stream, and client SDKs either dropping the resumed segments or rendering duplicates.

Observed scope: ~0.12% of long-running streaming sessions in the past 30 days (token sequences > 1024). Higher incidence under tenant-throttling events and brief gateway restarts. Dedicated/private deployments show fewer occurrences but are vulnerable to the same edge-case when the client reconnects to a different pod.

Root cause hypothesis: We currently treat streaming sessions as best-effort with an ephemeral session ID and a per-connection watermark. When a reconnect occurs to a different connection, late-emitted chunks lack durable attribution metadata (opaque session + sufficient sequence context). The combination of: (1) non-deterministic per-pod sequence assignment, (2) missing stable content-hash for fragment dedupe, and (3) a narrow in-memory backfill window, causes either dropped late chunks or duplicated tokens on resume.

Goal: Implement a deterministic server-side 'snapback' reconciliation mechanism plus an optional SDK-assisted resume handshake so late chunks are correctly attributed and stitched without user-visible duplication. We aim to reduce customer-facing truncated/duplicate stream incidents to <0.01% for hosted SSE and provide a migration path for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted SSE: reconnect + late-chunk injection test produces deterministic stitched transcript without duplicates for 99.99% of synthetic runs (sequences up to 4096 tokens)
SDKs: new resume handshake (resume_token) accepted by JS and Python SDKs and documented in release notes
Telemetry: new Grafana dashboard shows per-tenant late-chunk rate and snapback success rate
Feature flag: sse.snapback_enabled defaults off for 48-hour canary, then rolled to 100% after monitoring window
implementation_notes: Introduce stable session namespace: generate a globally-unique session_id at generation start and store durable session metadata in Redis with TTL aligned to resume window
Attach per-chunk metadata: sequence_number (monotonic), chunk_hash (SHA256 of payload), and global_offset to every SSE event emitted

Server-side reconciliation: on resume, client sends resume_token (session_id + last_seen_offset). Server replays any buffered chunks and accepts late chunks up to a configurable snapback_window_ms (default 15s or 50 tokens)
Idempotency: reject chunks with duplicate (session_id, sequence_number, chunk_hash) and log duplicates with debug-level correlation IDs
Memory tradeoff: move short-term buffers to a sharded Redis LRU system to limit per-pod memory; tune eviction to preserve snapshots for high-traffic tenants
SDK change: JS/Python SDKs expose .resume(resume_token) which performs handshake and exposes 'stitch_hint' events so apps can present deterministic merging to users
Backward compatibility: if client does not support resume_token, server falls back to conservative truncation (append special sentinel event 'RESUME_INCOMPATIBLE')
Config flagging: implement sse.snapback_enabled per-tenant to allow enterprise testing and Dedicated/Private staged rollouts
Additional safety: cap snapback window by token count and wall clock to avoid reordering large historical output
qa_plan: Unit tests for chunk dedupe, sequence monotonicity, and chunk_hash collision handling
Integration tests simulating pod restart + reconnect on different pod with 0-5s network jitter and random late chunks
Chaos test: induce gateway pod restarts during streaming at scale (k6 harness) and verify stitch rate <0.01% failure
Client SDK e2e: JS SDK resume and stitch example demo validated by QA engineer
Manual verification with affected customers (Acme Payments) on staging before production rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary 48h): enable sse.snapback_enabled for 1% of hosted traffic (low-risk tenants). Monitor snapback_success_rate, CPU, Redis usage.
Phase 2 (Ramp 3 days): expand to 25% after no regressions; enable SDK beta and invite key customers to trial
Phase 3 (Full): 100% hosted after 72h stable; offer configuration knobs for Dedicated/Private customers and publish migration guide
Rollback: feature-flag off + backfill job to annotate affected sessions; immediate rollback if error rate increases >200% or tail latency increases >25%
telemetry_and_dashboards: Sentry: stream-stitch-error-tagged events with session_id and tenant_id
Billing: track additional Redis egress and CPU under feature flag to ensure cost visibility
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increased Redis usage and potential latency for high concurrency tenants — mitigated via sharded LRU and per-tenant caps
Longer end-to-end latency for resumed streams due to reconciliation step (expected +5-25ms median); we will gate this behind canary and measure tail latency
SDK adoption burden: apps need to update to consume resume_token for best experience; fallback is conservative but may truncate in older clients
Edge case: if a late chunk arrives after the snapback_window, it will be dropped and logged — we will size window to balance memory and customer outcomes
comments: 2025-02-18 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after emergency call with Acme Payments. Attached initial repro snippet and sample transcript. Assigning to Liam for triage.

2025-02-19 Liam Chen: Root-cause hypothesis updated after reviewing pod logs — sequence numbers are per-connection not global. Proposed approach: stable session_id + chunk_hash for dedupe. Added dependency on ENG-271828 for adaptive session grace behavior.
2025-02-21 Design feedback (Priya Patel): Prefer explicit resume_token UX over silent resume to make failure modes visible to app developers. Recommend SDK event for 'stitch_hint'.
2025-02-24 Reliability review (Rohit Kapoor): Raised concern about Redis scaling. Suggested sharded LRU and per-tenant quota. Added telemetry requirement to monitor eviction rates.

2025-02-26 QA note (Morgan Lee): Integration tests added to pipeline. Reproduction harness simulates late-chunk arrival at 50ms-10s intervals. Found duplicate-chunk scenario when sequence wrap occurs at 32-bit counter — switching to 64-bit sequence numbers.
2025-03-01 Engineering update (Liam Chen): Draft server changes pushed to feature branch. Memory overhead measured +2.3% on canary pod with 1% traffic. Starting 48h canary next release window.
2025-03-02 PM update (Sofia Nguyen): Communicated planned canary to impacted customers and scheduled follow-up call post-canary. Added deadline to due_date.
